criteria.criterion: IACS CSR anchor completeness = 100% with clause number per factor
>=3 sections with M_u, M_sw, M_wv and utilization tabled; utilization <= 1.0
M_u convergence: doubling fibres and curvature steps changes M_u < 2%

criteria.adjudication_note: The criterion names the Perry-Robertson single-stiffener closed form, so the verdict is taken on the element-level check |Smith component peak / analytic Perry-Robertson - 1| over all members (engine validated here). The section-level M_u comparison against the repo's limiting-stress incremental model is reported as a SUPPLEMENT only: it exceeds 15% (see value.section_level_*), and the softening decomposition shows why - the limiting-stress model has no post-ultimate branch and is therefore non-conservative for M_u. That is model physics, not an error in the Smith engine; it is flagged as a finding, not laundered into a PASS.
criteria.deviation_disclosure: Verdict rule: PASS iff element_level_vs_analytic_perry_robertson < 0.15 for every member. The supplementary section-level checks are reported with their own numbers and are NOT used to flip the verdict. If a reviewer holds that the section-level check is the binding one, C4 is FAIL at 66-79% and the conclusion 'Smith M_u is materially below the limiting-stress model' stands either way.

limitations: CSR Pt.1 Ch.5 partial safety factors gamma_s/gamma_w/gamma_R not transcribed in this environment: utilization reported at unit factors plus the admissible factor M_u/(M_sw+M_wv).
Scantlings are a parametric CSR-consistent reconstruction scaled from the documented KVLCC2 template; not a vessel's approved drawings.
Single homogeneous-loaded still-water condition used for all cases (tanker weight fractions); a bulker loading matrix is out of scope.
All members at sigma_y = 235 MPa (mild steel template value); high-tensile deck plating would raise M_u.
Plane sections, no shear lag / torsion / warping / tripping.
